what: TEXTUAL VARIANTS: where the corpus tells the same matter two or more ways, each reading anchored to the line that says it. Tolkien wrote the legendarium repeatedly over fifty years and Christopher Tolkien published the layers; this dataset exists so that the archive can say THIS text says one thing and THAT text says another, without either being erased and without a winner being computed.

the_tradition_axis.what: WHICH TEXT a reading comes from, as a registered id -- not which VOLUME, and not which tier. map/traditions.py holds the register and is the only resolver.
the_tradition_axis.why: §X.4 asks for a textual-variant database and §I.3 demands that Tolkien's lifetime publications, his posthumous writings and CHRISTOPHER TOLKIEN'S EDITORIAL SELECTIONS AND ARRANGEMENTS be separately queryable. The archive's own coverage report has stood at a finding that §I.3's separation here is VOLUME-level only -- that nothing separates Christopher's commentary from his father's draft inside one HoMe file. On these readings it now does, because a hand read each line and named the text in `witness`; this key is that sentence normalised, and 8 readings of the 55 are Christopher's editorial matter distinguished from his father's text inside one volume.
the_tradition_axis.not_derived_from: the volume, the filename or the tier. C517: a t1 FILE is not t1 throughout -- 21 of 30 spans graded as Tolkien's own words were somebody else's book title printed inside a t1 volume, and t1_13_index.txt is wholly Christopher's index.
the_tradition_axis.refused: map/traditions.py REFUSES by name the strings that name a volume rather than a text -- UT, MR, HoME XI, HoME XII (PoME) -- and the bare title `Tale of Years`, which is LotR Appendix B AND the later Beleriandic annals at once. Each refusal is published there with what would settle it.
the_tradition_axis.null_means: the text takes two of §IV's nineteen values at once and neither is chosen. It never means nobody looked.

principle: SAMSI §X.4, executing the protocol's second non-negotiable principle -- do not collapse Tolkien's textual variants into a single simplified canon. Conflicting claims are held as PARALLEL ASSERTIONS (§I.7): every reading carries its own locus, tier and confidence, and none is subordinated to another by this file.

the_ruling.where: DECISIONS.md -- C366, his ruling of 25 August 2026
the_ruling.his_words: the latest published form is canon, or the one that Tolkien or his son said to be canon.
the_ruling.what_it_owes: C366 records that no canon-standing field existed anywhere in the archive and that the rule's own prescription -- a superseded reading stays, labelled as superseded, with its date -- had nowhere to be written down. This dataset is that place.
clauses_wired_in: (1) NEITHER CLAUSE RANKS. No record here computes a winner; `adjudication` is null unless a person decided, and then it names who and where.
(2) PUBLISHED MEANS THE LAST AUTHORIAL STATE, NOT THE LATEST PRINT DATE. Every `later_state` rests on a statement in the corpus by Tolkien or Christopher Tolkien, quoted and anchored.
(3) THE RULE DOES NOT FIRE WHERE THE SOURCE DECLINES TO CHOOSE; R12b governs -- show the disagreement. Those records carry `declines` with the refusing sentence verbatim.

how: Every reading's `q` is sought with map/ardatext.py -- the archive's one quote matcher -- and the LINE PUBLISHED IN `src` IS THE LINE THAT MATCHER RETURNED. No line number in this file was counted by hand or by a second reader: the corpus is mixed NFC/NFD and carries form feeds, so Python's splitlines() and grep -n disagree by hundreds of lines in a single volume. A span that does not verify is not published as a reading; it is published in `refused`.

vocabulary.conf_field: ruling 1's six, bare: C, I-H, I-M, I-L, EXT, NEO. `conf` grades the EVIDENCE for a reading -- how plainly the cited line says it -- and never its standing in the legendarium. A reading marked [C] is one the text states outright; it is not 'the canon one'.
vocabulary.date_conf_field: carried where the variant is about a DATE or a duration, in the same six values, under the owner's ruling of 11 August 2026.
vocabulary.refused: `C?` was named in this file's commission and is NOT used. map/confvocab_check.py is a per-dataset ratchet -- nine datasets carry unruled `conf` values under a declared debt and a dataset not already carrying the fault may not start -- so a new dataset writing `C?` would turn that guard red on its first run. The archive's own reading of `C?` is that it was invented because the ruled six cannot express canon standing, which is the gap C366 left open. Widening the vocabulary is a RULING, not a side effect of landing a dataset.

no_adjudication_rule: A variant is NOT resolved here unless a person resolved it, and then the record names who, where it is written, and what it says. Two of the records carry an adjudication and neither is this archive's: one is the owner's, one is the author's own designation in the Prologue to The Lord of the Rings. Where the archive cannot tell which reading is later, `later_state.known` is false and the reason is stated. THAT IS A MEASURED SILENCE AND IT IS HONEST.
silences_rule: A silence may only be asserted by something that looked. Every entry in `silences` carries the probe, the population it was put to, and what came back.
